outline.title: The Unpublished
outline.premise: In Santiago, Chile, in the tense months before September 1973, investigative journalist Valentina Reyes obtains irrefutable documentary proof of CIA coordination with Chilean military officers planning a coup against President Allende. She races to publish her findings, but every editor she approaches — intimidated, complicit, or simply afraid — turns her away, leaving her holding a truth that the world is not yet willing to print.
themes: The weaponization of silence against inconvenient truth
Institutional cowardice as a form of political violence
The personal cost of bearing witness in a collapsing democracy
Complicity by omission in the machinery of power

characters.name: Valentina Reyes
characters.role: Protagonist — investigative journalist at a Santiago daily newspaper
characters.arc: Begins believing that truth, once documented, is unstoppable; ends understanding that truth without a vessel is just another casualty of power, and chooses to preserve the evidence at devastating personal cost.

characters.name: Rodrigo Fuentes
characters.role: Valentina's editor at El Diario del Sur, a centrist newspaper
characters.arc: Starts as a mentor who prizes journalistic courage, but reveals himself to be a man whose principles dissolve the moment his family's safety is threatened.

characters.name: Comandante Héctor Vidal
characters.role: Mid-ranking Chilean Army officer and Valentina's clandestine source
characters.arc: A conflicted insider who hands Valentina the documents out of conscience, then is disappeared before he can corroborate her story publicly.

characters.name: Margaret Holt
characters.role: Santiago bureau chief for an American wire service
characters.arc: Presents herself as a fellow truth-seeker but ultimately protects her access and career over the story, embodying the foreign press's complicity.

characters.name: Tomás Reyes
characters.role: Valentina's younger brother, a student activist
characters.arc: His arrest by plainclothes security forces becomes the lever that forces Valentina to choose between publishing and his survival.

chapters.title: The Documents
chapters.beat: Valentina receives a cache of classified cables from Comandante Vidal proving CIA coordination with coup plotters, and her editor Rodrigo initially agrees to run the story — the ordinary world of a functioning, if fragile, press cracks open with possibility.
chapters.arc_notes: Act I — Setup: Ordinary world established (Santiago's embattled free press in mid-1973), inciting incident delivered (Vidal hands over the documents), and First Plot Point reached when Rodrigo gives conditional approval to publish, committing Valentina irrevocably to the story.

chapters.title: Every Door Closes
chapters.beat: Rodrigo kills the story under pressure from the paper's owners, Vidal vanishes after a midnight arrest, and Margaret Holt at the American wire service declines to run the cables — then Tomás is detained, and a security agent makes clear that Valentina's brother's fate is tied to her silence.
chapters.arc_notes: Act II — Confrontation: Early obstacles escalate (Rodrigo's betrayal, Vidal's disappearance, Margaret's refusal) through the Midpoint reversal (Vidal's arrest transforms the story from a publishing problem into a survival crisis and confirms the coup's machinery is already in motion) to the Second Plot Point / darkest moment (Tomás's detention strips Valentina of every ally and forces an impossible choice).

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.beat: On the morning of September 11, 1973, as jets circle La Moneda, Valentina surrenders the documents to a Swedish embassy contact for safekeeping rather than destroy them to save Tomás — Tomás is eventually released, the story goes unpublished for years, but the cables survive.
chapters.arc_notes: Act III — Resolution: Climax arrives when Valentina chooses preservation over immediate publication (transformation made visible — she has moved from believing truth must be heard now to understanding that truth must first survive), and the resolution closes on the documents sealed in a diplomatic pouch, the coup's smoke rising outside, and Valentina walking toward the detention center to find her brother — closure that is earned but not triumphant.
